mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate environment, as indicated by FEDFUNDS below 1.0%, reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises by >0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand in the housing and retail sectors, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, indicating a contraction in manufacturing output, the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days as investors factor in reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened investor confidence in corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate is above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises by >0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) from the prior month indicates a labor market contraction coupled with manufacturing weakness, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both UNRATE and INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: When residential sales (RSAFS) exceed $470 billion (470,000 million dollars), it signals strong consumer demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the economy benefits from robust consumer spending.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 470000.
